channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Fight over funding for Iran war could put the government at risk of a shutdown
item.description: The government runs out of funding on December 11 and funding for the war in Iran could prove decisive in whether negotiations end with a deal or another shutdown.
item.content:encoded: The government runs out of funding on December 11 and funding for the war in Iran could prove decisive in whether negotiations end with a deal or another shutdown.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Grisales

item.title: GOP Sen. Johnson rejects tying government funding to an end to the Iran war
item.description: "We're not going to shut down the war," Sen. Ron Johnson said as Republicans and Democrats struggle to reach a government funding deal.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Critics are worried about Anthropic's influence after first day of public trading
item.description: Anthropic's initial public offering was a success for shareholders, including its founders. But there were also protests about whether the company can be a responsible steward of AI technology.
item.content:encoded: Anthropic's initial public offering was a success for shareholders, including its founders. But there were also protests about whether the company can be a responsible steward of AI technology.
item.dc:creator: Shannon Bond

item.title: Experts say powering data centers uses more water than cooling them
item.description: Fears about data center water use are especially acute in Arizona. But keeping servers cool uses a lot less water than generating the electricity for which data centers are so thirsty.
item.content:encoded: Fears about data center water use are especially acute in Arizona. But keeping servers cool uses a lot less water than generating the electricity for which data centers are so thirsty.
item.dc:creator: Alex Hager

item.title: Morning news brief
item.description: Without funding deal, the government could shut down next month, Silicon Valley and national security community bump heads on efforts to restrict U.S. tech to China, Army delays detonation in Iowa.

item.title: 'I Play Rocky' chronicles Sylvester Stallone's unconventional road to stardom
item.description: Sylvester Stallone's unlikely rise to stardom is dramatized in the new film "I Play Rocky." NPR's A Martinez speaks with director Peter Farrelly and the man playing Sly, Anthony Ippolito.

item.title: AI models are propelling rapid growth and revealing vulnerabilities
item.description: AI models are exposing the internet's longstanding insecurity, driving rapid change and technical outages.
item.content:encoded: AI models are exposing the internet's longstanding insecurity, driving rapid change and technical outages.

item.title: How creators are adapting to the changing television landscape
item.description: Everything about making TV shows has changed dramatically in the last 15 years. TV writer and producer Mike Schur explains how streaming changed TV economics, and how creators are adapting.

item.title: Can incoming Democratic-run Congress circumvent Trump's veto threats?
item.description: How can the incoming Congress deliver on voters' wishes under threat of a presidential veto? NPR's Steve Inskeep asks John Lawrence, former chief of staff to former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi.

item.title: European-Japanese space mission will soon reach its final destination -- Mercury
item.description: A joint European-Japanese space mission known as BepiColombo is about to reach its destination, Mercury, to study the innermost planet of our solar system.
